Beállítom Oroszország egy napon belül háromszor támadta csütörtökön Kijevet, miután este újabb légicsapásokat hajtottak végre az ukrán főváros ellen, ahol a legfrissebb, péntek reggeli hivatalos ukrán közlés szerint 16-an haltak meg, és 42-en megsebesültek. Moszkva csütörtökre virradó éjszaka drónokkal, ballisztikus rakétákkal és cirkálórakétákkal indított nagy, több órán át tartó támadást Kijev ellen, majd napközben egy másodikat. Közben Oroszország több mint ezer támadást hajtott végre 24 óra alatt a Zaporizzsjai terület több mint ötven település ellen, amikben négyen sérültek meg, az Ukrinform ukrán hírügynökség beszámolója szerint. A támadások döntő többségét, majdnem nyolcszázat drónokkal hajtották végre. Péntekre virradó éjszaka ketten haltak meg orosz támadásokban Harkiv környékén. Közben orosz dróntámadás ért egy moldovai-ukrán határátkelőt is, amit ideiglenesen le kellett zárni. Az ukrán hadsereg pénteken az orosz Lukoil második legnagyobb olajfinomítója ellen hajtott végre támadást Perm városánál – írta az ukrán sajtó. A beszámolók szerint a helyiek által készített videókon robbanásokat lehet látni, valamint azt, hogy füst száll fel a finomítóból. Permnél drónriadót hirdettek , és a helyi repülőtéren korlátozták a gépek indulását és érkezését. A PNOS finomító a Lukoil második legnagyobb olajfinomítója és egyike a tíz legnagyobb finomítónak Oroszországban – írta a Kyiv Post. Az üzemet áprilisban, májusban és júniusban is támadta Ukrajna, ami egyre több támadást hajt végre az orosz energetikai infrastruktúra ellen. Az orosz védelmi minisztérium közlése szerint péntekre virradó éjszaka 325 ukrán drónt lőttek le Oroszország felett, köztük Moszkva környékén, valamint a Fekete-tengernél. Speaking after a Council of the Baltic Sea States meeting in Warsaw attended by Ukraine’s Foreign Minister Andriy Sybiha and EU High Representative Kaja Kallas, Sikorski warned that no diplomatic solution can be imposed on Kyiv without its consent. by TVP World | Nov. 7, 2026, 9:00 am Flip Share Facebook X (Twitter) LinkedIn Bluesky Email Copy Copied Poland’s Foreign Minister Radosław Sikorski speaks during a plenary session of the G20 Foreign Ministers’ Meeting in Atlanta, Georgia, Oct. 30, 2026. (Photo by Erik S. Lesser / AFP) Content Share Facebook X (Twitter) LinkedIn Bluesky Email Copy Copied Flip Poland will provide an additional 8 million zlotys ($2 million) to help buy generators for Ukraine ahead of winter, Foreign Minister Radosław Sikorski said on Friday, as countries in the region pledged to strengthen military and financial support for Kyiv. Speaking after a meeting of the Council of the Baltic Sea States in Warsaw, Sikorski said the gathering had confirmed regional unity in the face of Russia’s ongoing aggression. JOIN US ON TELEGRAM Follow our coverage of the war on the @Kyivpost_official . He also stressed that Ukraine must have a say in any negotiations over its future, warning that no settlement could be imposed on the embattled country without its consent. “Ukraine should not negotiate its future under the pressure of shelling against civilians,” Sikorski said. Advertisement “No solution can be imposed on Ukraine without its consent and presence at the table,” he added, arguing that European security must also not be discussed without the involvement of countries most exposed to the consequences of a potential deal with Russia . His comments came days before US-mediated talks between Ukrainian and Russian negotiators in Abu Dhabi on November 10-11. The working-level meeting is expected to focus on ending the war, post-conflict security arrangements, de-escalation and humanitarian measures. It will be the first round of US-brokered talks since February, when the process was suspended after the US and Israel went to war with Iran. Other Topics of Interest Russian Drones Hit One of Ukraine's Oldest Oil Extraction Plants Russian drones critically damaged the historic Nizhyn Fat and Oil Plant on Nov. 10, adding to over 100 attacks on Chernihiv agricultural sites in 2026. Ukrainian Foreign Minister Andrii Sybiha and EU foreign policy chief Kaja Kallas also attended Friday’s meeting in Warsaw, where preparing for Abu Dhabi was on the agenda. The Council of the Baltic Sea States is a forum for cooperation among the countries around the Baltic. Ukraine is an observer. Russia, a founding member, left in 2022 after being suspended over its full-scale invasion of Ukraine. Military drills Sikorski said Poland was ready to contribute to future efforts to secure peace. Advertisement He pointed to military exercises next week involving the so-called coalition of the willing, a group of more than 30 mostly European countries led by Britain and France that is planning security guarantees for Ukraine. The drills, called Koalicja (“Coalition”), will run from Nov. 9 to 22 at Nowa Dęba in southeastern Poland. Thousands of troops from 11 countries will take part, alongside Ukrainian soldiers. The US is not involved. The exercise is the first large-scale test of whether a potential multinational force drawn from the coalition’s members could deploy to Ukraine once a ceasefire takes effect. The force would aim to deter Russia from resuming the war, help protect Ukraine’s skies and sea routes, and help rebuild its armed forces. Poland was chosen as host partly because much of Western aid to Ukraine passes through its territory. Estonia prepares to close all five road border crossings with Russia Copy/paste the link below: Copy Copy/paste the article video embed link below: Copy Updated: 27 November 2026 - 9:57 GMT+1 Long queues have formed at Estonia's border with Russia ahead of its planned closure on 1 December. The decision, prompted by security concerns, threatens to separate families and disrupt local businesses. … More For families living on either side of the Estonian-Russian border , the impending closure threatens months of separation . People carrying suitcases queued at the Friendship Bridge linking Narva and Ivangorod , rushing to visit relatives before restrictions take effect. Some had given up their jobs in Estonia to be closer to elderly parents in Russia . ADVERTISEMENT ADVERTISEMENT The closure follows sabotage attacks targeting Estonia’s defence industry , attributed by its security services to Russian intelligence . Moscow dismisses the allegations as unfounded and accuses Tallinn of seeking to erect a new “Iron Curtain” . Beyond the human cost, the decision threatens businesses dependent on cross-border travel. Local authorities estimate annual revenue losses of between €500,000 and €600,000 for Narva and Setomaa , while the government is preparing a €2 million support package over six months . All five road crossings will shut at 7am on 1 December for an initial six months , with rail freight through Narva continuing subject to sanctions. Around 3,000 people have signed a petition calling for exemptions on family grounds, particularly for those with sick or elderly relatives. The government will review the situation after six months .
